l.i: Annua Six rediens Siderat illa dies:
En aliam AEmylia nobis, aliumque Melissum,
Mox Syno in puero reddidit alma Venus.
Fortunate puer, patrio cui melle lepores
Et quem materno condita lepore Melissus
Mella inter genuit, melleus ipse pater.
At tu, Christe, istos isto cum melle lepores
Melle tuo condi, merge lepore tuo.

main_text.l: OVa prius immensi qua qua patet area caeli,
Libera qua soluit parte volabat avis,
Clausa licet cauea tam stricto carcere, fortis
Nec commutata signa dat Ulla sua,
Nec captiua filet, toto sed gutture lata

l.i: At tu, pro Christo qui corpore clausus, apertas
Mente vides caeli liberiore fores, Et
Pene ipso calcas limina sacra pede,
Num vel corde pauens, vel maestus voce filebis?
Nec potius facies qua tibi mostrat anus?

page.notes: Greek title word partly illegible in the scan; the verse is set in italic with a long s. Several letters in the first poem's block are doubtful (e.g. "Syno", "Sixrediens"), and the decorative initial O is read as "O". Possible printing errors left as printed.
